We did not see the Person, our sight taken by that splendour; then knowledge born of the god's yoga appeared to us.
mahabharata:12:323.30	One who has not practised austerity cannot easily see him; so, practising great austerity for another hundred years suited to the time,
mahabharata:12:323.31	at the end of the vow we saw very beautiful men, white, moon-like, marked with all auspicious signs,
mahabharata:12:323.32	with joined palms constantly, muttering Brahman, facing east and north; that mental muttering was muttered by those great souls, and by that one-pointed mind Hari is pleased.
mahabharata:12:323.33	Whatever radiance there would be, tiger among sages, of the sun at the end of an age, such was the radiance of each one of those men.
mahabharata:12:323.34	We thought that island a dwelling of splendour; none there was greater, all of equal splendour.
mahabharata:12:323.35	Then, Brihaspati, we suddenly saw the radiance of a thousand suns arisen at once.
mahabharata:12:323.36	Then those men together ran swiftly, with joined palms, glad, saying only 'Homage!'
mahabharata:12:323.37	Then, as they greeted, we heard a vast sound: an offering was being made by those men to that god.
mahabharata:12:323.38	But we, our minds suddenly taken by his splendour, saw nothing at all, our sight, strength and senses taken.
mahabharata:12:323.39	One cry alone was heard uttered by us without pause: 'You have conquered, lotus-eyed one; homage to you, maker of the universe.
mahabharata:12:323.40	Homage to you, Hrishikesha, great Person, first-born'; this sound was heard by us, uttered in the letters of phonetics.
mahabharata:12:323.41	In the meantime a pure wind bearing every scent carried divine flowers and herbs fit for rites.
mahabharata:12:323.42	Hari, worshipped five times a day by those single-minded men, surely came there, as the voice was uttered by them; but we did not see him, bewildered by his illusion.
mahabharata:12:323.43	When the wind had ceased and the offering had been made, our minds became disturbed with worry, best of the Angirases.
mahabharata:12:323.44	Among those thousands of men of pure birth, none honoured us in mind or with his eye.
mahabharata:12:323.45	Those troops of sages too, self-possessed, devoted to oneness, did not show regard to us, being engaged in Brahman-regard.
mahabharata:12:323.46	Then, as we were exhausted and also wasted by austerity, a certain bodiless being, self-possessed, spoke to us:
mahabharata:12:323.47	'You have seen the white men, devoid of all senses; by seeing these, the lord of gods is seen, best of the twice-born.
mahabharata:12:323.48	Go, sages, all of you, as you came, soon from here; he cannot in any way be seen by one who is not a devotee.
mahabharata:12:323.49	By great time, those who have attained single-mindedness may, if they wish, see the blessed one, hard to see with his disc of radiance.
mahabharata:12:323.50	But you, best of the twice-born, have a great task to do: from now, when the Krita age has passed and has gone to reversal,
mahabharata:12:323.51	in the Vaivasvata interval, brahmanas, when the Treta age has come, you will be helpers for the accomplishment of the gods' purpose.'
mahabharata:12:323.52	Hearing that wonderful speech, Soma-drinker, by his grace we easily reached the place we wished.
mahabharata:12:323.53	Thus, though with good austerity and with offerings to gods and ancestors, the god was not seen by us; how then can you hope to see Narayana, the great being, maker of the universe, enjoyer of offerings to gods and ancestors?
[Bhishma said:] Thus with Ekata's word and Dvita's and Trita's opinion, and consoled by the assembly members, the noble-minded Brihaspati gathered the sacrifice and worshipped the deity.
His sacrifice completed, King Vasu ruled the people; fallen from heaven by a brahmin's curse, he then entered the earth.
Gone beneath the earth, ever fond of dharma, devoted to Narayana, he sang Narayana's praise.
By his grace alone he rose again, went from the earth and soon reached the abode of Brahma, the supreme goal, as it is said, readily.
[Bhishma said:] On this too they recite this ancient Itihasa, the dialogue of the sages and the gods, Bharata.
One must sacrifice with the aja, the gods said to the best of the twice-born; the aja is to be understood as the goat, no other animal; so the rule stands.
[The sages said:] "One must sacrifice with seeds at sacrifices": thus the Vedic scripture. Seeds are called aja; you should not kill a goat.
Dharma of the good is not where an animal is killed, gods; this is the best, the Krita age; how should an animal be slain?
[Bhishma said:] As the sages were thus conversing with the gods, the best of kings, Vasu, came by the road to that place, moving in the sky, glorious, with his whole army and vehicles.
Seeing Vasu suddenly coming through the sky, the twice-born said to the gods: "This king will surely settle the doubt.
A sacrificer, the best giver, fond of the good of all beings: how could this great Vasu say otherwise?"
Having agreed thus, the gods and sages suddenly approached King Vasu and asked him.
Our side, king, is that one must sacrifice with grains; the gods' side, king, is the animal; tell us.
[Bhishma said:] Knowing the gods' view, Vasu, resorting to their side, said then that one must sacrifice with the goat, the aja.
Then all those sages, radiant as the sun, angry, said to Vasu, who stood in his car speaking for the gods' side:
Since you have taken the gods' side, fall from heaven; from today, king, your course is blocked in the sky; struck by our curse, you will break the earth and enter it.
Then in that very moment the king Uparichara quickly went down into a cleft of the earth; but memory did not leave him, by Narayana's command.
And all the gods together, unagitated, considered how to free Vasu from the curse, for the king had good deeds.
This great-souled king has got a curse on our account; we dwellers of heaven together must do something dear to him.
Having so resolved quickly, the lords went and, glad in mind, spoke to King Uparichara then:

You are devoted to the god, friend of brahmanas, Hari, teacher of gods and asuras; may he, pleased, as he wishes, free you from the curse.
mahabharata:12:324.21	But the great souls, the twice-born, must be honoured; their austerity must surely bear fruit, best of kings.
mahabharata:12:324.22	Because you fell suddenly from the sky to the surface of the earth, we give you one favour, best of kings.
mahabharata:12:324.23	For as long a time as you remain under the fault of the curse, becoming a cow of the earth's cleft for that time, you will receive the stream of ghee well offered by great-souled brahmanas at sacrifices.
mahabharata:12:324.24	You will obtain it through our meditation, and let no weariness touch you; hunger and thirst, lord of kings, will not be in the cleft of the earth.
mahabharata:12:324.25	Having drunk Vasu's stream and being nourished by splendour, that god, pleased with our boon, will go to Brahma's world.
Having thus given the boon to the king, all the dwellers of heaven, the gods and the ascetic sages, went to their own homes.
He constantly paid worship to Vishvaksena, Bharata, and constantly muttered the prayer issued from Narayana's mouth.
There too, scourge of foes, though in the cleft of the earth, he worshipped Hari, lord of gods, with five sacrifices at the five times.
Then the blessed Narayana Hari, pleased with his devotion, for one who was devoted to none other, intent on him, self-controlled,
the boon-giving blessed Vishnu, to the best of the twice-born near him, Garuda of great speed, appeared, smiling as it were.

Best of the twice-born, greatly fortunate, go at my word: the sovereign king named Vasu, righteous-souled, has taken refuge in me.
mahabharata:12:324.32	Entering the earth's surface through the anger of brahmanas, the lords of brahmanas were honoured; but you go, best of the twice-born.
mahabharata:12:324.33	Garuda, by my command, hidden in the cleft of the earth, make the best of kings, who goes below, a sky-goer quickly.
Then Garuda, spreading his wings, swift as the wind, entered the cleft of the earth where Vasu stayed silent.
Then suddenly lifting him up, the son of Vinata swiftly rose to the sky and released him there.
In that very moment Uparichara was born again, and the best of kings went bodily to Brahma's world.
Thus, Kaunteya, by a fault of speech and by the gods' command, a goal fit for a non-sacrificer was got by that great soul through the brahmins' curse.
Only because the Person, Hari the lord, was served by him, he soon left the curse and reached Brahma's world.
All this has been told to you, how those beings were men, and how the sage Narada went to the white island; all that I shall tell you; listen with one mind, king.
Somewhere pure as the moon, somewhere more distinguished than the moon, somewhere fire-coloured, somewhere shaped like a sacrificial hearth, the lord:
somewhere parrot-feather coloured, somewhere crystal-bright, somewhere like a heap of dark collyrium, somewhere shining like gold,
somewhere of coral-sprout colour, somewhere white, somewhere gold-hued, somewhere like beryl,
somewhere like dark beryl, somewhere like sapphire, somewhere like a peacock's neck, somewhere like a pearl necklace.
Bearing these many colours in form, the eternal one, thousand-eyed, glorious, hundred-headed, thousand-footed,
thousand-bellied and thousand-armed, and in places unmanifest, uttering Om from his mouth, and after it the Savitri,
and from his other mouths the wealth drawn from the four Vedas, the Aranyaka, the self-controlled god Hari Narayana sang.
The lord of gods, lord of sacrifice, then held in his hands an altar, a water-pot, kusha grass, stones in the form of jewels, a black-antelope skin, a staff, and blazing fire.
Narada, best of the twice-born, pleased, with pleased self, silent and pure, bowed to the Supreme Lord; and to him bowing his head, the imperishable first of the gods spoke:

Ekata, Dvita and Trita, the great sages, came to this place longing to see me.
mahabharata:12:326.12	They did not see me, nor will anyone, except the best of the single-minded; and you are held to be single-minded.
mahabharata:12:326.13	These excellent forms of mine were born in the house of Dharma, Brahmana; always serve them and accomplish what you came for.
mahabharata:12:326.14	And choose a boon from me, Brahmana, whatever you wish here; I am pleased with you today, here, the imperishable one in universal form.
[Narada said:] "Today the fruit of my austerity, my restraints and observances, god, has been gained at once, since I have seen the blessed one.
This is my utmost boon, that I have seen you, the eternal, blessed, all-seeing lion, all-formed, the great lord."
[Bhishma said:] Having thus shown himself to Narada, Parameshthi's son, he spoke again: "Go, Narada, without delay.
These devotees of mine, without sense-food, moon-radiant, one-pointed, think of me; let there be no obstacle to them.
These greatly fortunate ones were single-minded of old and are perfected; freed from tamas and rajas, they will doubtless enter me.
He who is not to be seen by the eye, nor touched by touch, nor smelt by smell, free of taste,
whom sattva, rajas and tamas, the qualities, do not approach, who is all-pervading, the witness, called the self of the world,
does not perish when the bodies of the host of beings perish; unborn, eternal, everlasting, without qualities and without parts,
famed as the twenty-fifth beyond twice twelve principles, the Person, inactive, and said to be seen by knowledge:
entering whom the freed here become so, best of the twice-born; know him as Vasudeva, the eternal Supreme Self.
See the greatness and majesty of the god, Narada, who is never stained by good or bad deeds.
Sattva, rajas and tamas: they call these the qualities; these stand and move in all bodies.
The knower of the field enjoys these qualities but is not enjoyed by them; without qualities, an enjoyer of qualities, creator of qualities, above qualities.
The earth, support of the world, divine sage, dissolves in water; water dissolves in light, and light dissolves in wind.
Wind goes to dissolution in space, and space in mind; for mind is the highest element, and it dissolves in the unmanifest.
The unmanifest dissolves in the Person, Brahmana, the inactive; there is nothing higher than that eternal Person.
There is no permanent being in the world, moving or unmoving, except that one eternal Person, Vasudeva; for Vasudeva of great strength is the self of all beings.
Earth, wind, space, water and light as fifth: these great ones together are called the body.
Brahmana, he who enters it, unseen and of light movement, the lord, only on its arising moves the body.
The body is never made without a collection of elements, and the elements, Brahmana, do not move without the living soul.
That soul is counted as Shesha, the lord Sankarshana; thus one may gain the state of Sanatkumara by one's own deed.
In whom all beings go to dissolution at the end, that is the mind of all beings, called Pradyumna.
From him is born the doer, the effect and the cause; from whom everything arises, the world moving and unmoving: he is Aniruddha, he is the ruler, he is manifestation in all actions.
Vasudeva the blessed, the knower of the field, whose self is without qualities, is to be known; he is the same as the blessed soul, the lord Sankarshana.
From Sankarshana Pradyumna, who is called the mind-being; and from Pradyumna, Aniruddha, who is the sense of ego, the great lord.
From me everything arises, the world moving and unmoving, the imperishable and the perishable, being and non-being, Narada.
Those who enter me become free here, and those who are my devotees; for I am to be known as the Person, the inactive twenty-fifth,

without qualities, without parts, without pairs, without possessions. You are not to know me as having form because I am seen so; if I wished, I could vanish in a moment; I am the lord, the teacher of the world.
This is illusion made by me, that you see me joined with the qualities of all beings, Narada; you should not so understand. I have rightly told you my fourfold form.
These greatly fortunate men, perfected, became single-minded, freed from tamas and rajas, and will enter me, sage.
I am the doer, the effect and the cause, Narada; I am what is called the soul, and the soul is established in me. Let no such thought arise in you that you have seen the soul by me.
I am all-pervading, Brahmana, the inner self of the host of beings; when the bodies of the host of beings perish, I do not perish.
Hiranyagarbha, the origin of the world, four-faced, called by name, Brahma, the eternal god, thinks of many purposes of mine.
See the eleven Rudras of mine standing on the right side, and the twelve Adityas standing on the left side.
In front of me see the eight Vasus, best of the gods, and behind see the Nasatya and Dasra, the physicians.
See all the Prajapatis, see the seven sages, see the Vedas and the sacrifices by the hundred, the nectar and the herbs.
See austerities and observances, and the restraints, of various kinds, and likewise lordship with its eight qualities, standing in one, embodied.
See Shri, Lakshmi, Kirti, the humped Earth, and the mother of the Vedas, the goddess Sarasvati, abiding in me.
See, Narada, the pole star, the best of luminaries, moving in the sky, the clouds, the oceans, lakes and rivers.
See, good one, the four troops of ancestors embodied, and these three qualities abiding in me without form.
Even above the rite for the gods, sage, the rite for the ancestors is distinguished; for I alone am from the beginning the father of the gods and of the ancestors.
Becoming Hayashiras in the north-west ocean, I drink the well-offered oblations and funeral offerings joined with faith.
Brahma, created by me of old, himself sacrificed to my sacrifice; then, pleased, I gave him the most excellent boons.
Being my son at the beginning of the age, and being the overseer of the world, and a name made by ego, a synonym.
The limit made by you no one will transgress, and you, Brahmana, will be a giver of boons to those who seek boons.
You will be worshipped always by troops of gods and asuras, by sages, by ancestors, ascetic, greatly fortunate one of sharp vows, and by various beings.
When I appear in the affairs of the gods, I am to be instructed by you, Brahmana, and to be employed like a son.
Having given Brahma of boundless splendour these and other lovely boons, I was pleased, and I became intent on withdrawal.
Extinction of all dharmas, withdrawal, is remembered as supreme; therefore one who has attained withdrawal should live content in every limb.
Teachers certain of Sankhya say that I am Kapila, dwelling in the sun, eternal, joined with knowledge as my companion.
This blessed Hiranyagarbha, well praised in the Veda, am I, Brahmana, the course of yoga named in the yoga treatises.
Having come to manifestation I stay in heaven forever; then, at the end of a thousand ages, I shall draw in the world again, placing beings, moving and unmoving, in myself.
Alone with knowledge I shall roam, best of the twice-born; then I shall make the whole world again here by knowledge.
That fourth form of mine created the imperishable Shesha; he is called Sankarshana, and he too begot Pradyumna.
From Pradyumna, Aniruddha am I; my creation is again and again; from Aniruddha, Brahma, the first one born of the lotus there.
From Brahma come all beings, moving and unmoving; know this creation, at the beginnings of ages again and again.
As Time, of boundless splendour, brings back by force the sun's rising and setting that were lost from the sky here, so by force, for the good of all beings, I
shall bring back the earth, lost, with all her limbs overwhelmed by beings, girdled by the sea, to her own place, taking the boar form.
I shall slay Hiranyaksha, the Daitya proud of his strength; again, taking the Narasimha form, for the gods' work I shall slay Hiranyakashipu, Diti's delight, the destroyer of sacrifices.
Bali, the mighty great asura, son of Virochana, will be, and will make Shakra fall from his own kingdom.
When the three worlds have been taken by him and the lord of Shachi is turned away, I shall be born as the twelfth son of Aditi from Kashyapa.
Then I shall give the kingdom to Shakra of boundless splendour and establish the gods in their own places, Narada, and make Bali dwell in the nether world.
In the Treta age I shall be Rama, the lifter of the line of Bhrigu, and shall uproot the kshatriyas, rich in strength and vehicles.
When the juncture of Treta and Dvapara has come, I shall be Rama, son of Dasharatha, lord of the world.
By the injury of Trita, Ekata and Dvita, sons of Prajapati, sages, will get deformity and the state of elephants.
Those born in their line, forest-dwellers, will be my helpers in the gods' work, Brahmana.
Then I shall slay in battle the terrible lord of rakshasas Ravana, the disgrace of Pulastya's family, with his host, the thorn of the world.
At the very end of the juncture of Dvapara and Kali, my manifestation will be at Mathura for the sake of Kamsa.
There, having slain very many danavas, thorns of the gods, I shall make Dvaraka city my dwelling at Kushasthali.
Living in that city, I shall slay what is hostile to Aditi, Naraka son of Bhumi, Mura, and the danava Pitha.
Having slain the best of the danavas, I shall bring the lovely Pragjyotisha city, rich in many riches, to Kushasthali.
I shall defeat Shankara and Mahasena, eager and honoured by the world of the gods, well-wishers of Bana.
Then, having conquered Bali's son Bana of a thousand arms, I shall destroy all the dwellers of Saubha.
Kalayavana, who is famed, enveloped in Garga's splendour, will have his death from me alone, best of the twice-born.
The mighty Jarasandha, enemy of all kings, will be an asura, a prosperous king at Girivraja; by the stirring of my mind his death will come.
When all the kings of the earth have assembled with their forces, Indra's son will be my one good helper.
So people will say: the sages Nara and Narayana, lords, bent on it, burn up the kshatriyas for the work of the world.
Having brought down the burden of the earth as desired, I shall make a terrible destruction of all the chief Satvatas and of Dvaraka, good one, destroying my own kinsmen.
Bearing the fourfold form, I shall do immeasurable deeds, and then go to my own worlds honoured by Brahma.

Hamsa and Hayashiras are manifestations, best of the twice-born; when the Veda and the sacred tradition were lost, I brought them back; and the Vedas and the tradition were made again in the Krita age before.
Those that are past are heard in the Puranas, or somewhere; many of my excellent manifestations have passed, and having done the world's work they return to their own nature.
Not even Brahma has gained such a sight of me as you have gained today here, with a mind gone to single-mindedness.
All this has been told to you, Brahmana, devoted one, by me, past and future, with its secret, good one."
Having said only this, the blessed god, bearing the universal form, the imperishable, vanished right there.
Narada too, of great splendour, having gained the desired grace, hurried to the Badari hermitage to see Nara and Narayana.
This great Upanishad, joined with the four Vedas, made of Sankhya and yoga, called by the name Pancharatra,
sung from Narayana's mouth, Narada recited again in Brahma's abode, dear one, as seen and as heard.
[Yudhishthira said:] This greatness of that wise one is truly wonderful. Does Brahma not know it, since he heard it from Narada?
The blessed grandfather is next to that god; how would he not know the power of the one of boundless might?
[Bhishma said:] Thousands of great ages and hundreds of great ages have passed, king, creations and dissolutions.
Brahma is remembered at the beginning of creation as the lord who makes creatures; he knows the best of gods, and still more, king, the Supreme Self, the ruler, and the origin of himself.
To the other crowds of Siddhas gathered in Brahma's abode he recited that Purana, equal to the Veda.
From them, the sun heard it, and recited it, Bharata, to the pure-souled followers of the self.
Sixty-six thousand sages of purified selves, who were created first, while the sun scorches the worlds: to all those pure-souled ones the sun told it.
By those great-souled sages who followed the sun, dear one, the gods gathered on Meru were made to hear this excellent teaching.
Then Asita the twice-born, best of sages, having heard it from the gods, recited it, king, to the ancestors.
My father Shantanu also told it to me, dear one; having heard it, I have recited it to you, Bharata.
Whether gods or sages, all who have heard this Purana worship the Supreme Self again and again.
This account, composed by sages and come down by tradition, you should not give, king, to one who is not a devotee of Vasudeva.
From me you have heard hundreds of other stories, king, of dharma; the essence of them has been drawn out in this one.
As nectar was drawn out by gods and asuras by churning, so this nectar of a story has been drawn out here by the brahmins.
The man who reads this always, or who hears this, gone to single-minded devotion, composed in solitude,
reaching the great white island, becoming moon-bright, will enter the god of a thousand rays; of this there is no doubt.
Hearing this story from the beginning, the afflicted is freed from disease, the seeker gains his wishes, and the devotee reaches the devotee's goal.
And you too, king, must always worship the Supreme Person; he is mother, father and teacher of the whole world.
May the god friend of brahmanas, the blessed eternal one, be pleased with you, Yudhishthira of mighty arms; Janardana is mighty-armed.
[Vaishampayana said:] Hearing this excellent account, Janamejaya, the king of dharma and all his brothers became devoted to Narayana.
Conquered by the blessed Person: so, Bharata, they were always devoted to muttering and uttering Sarasvati.
Our teacher, the best sage Krishna Dvaipayana, sang the supreme prayer, uttering Narayana.
Going constantly through the sky to the Milk Ocean, the abode of nectar, and having worshipped the lord of gods, he came back to his own hermitage.
[Janamejaya said:] The blessed lord himself, established in the dharma of withdrawal, secure, fond of devotees, ordains the dharmas of action.
How were the gods made worthy of shares in the dharmas of action, and how were the dharmas of withdrawal made, with minds turned away?
Cut this doubt for us, brahmana, this hidden eternal matter; you have told the story of Narayana, joined with dharma.
These worlds with Brahma, with gods, asuras and men, are seen everywhere attached to the rites told for prosperity; and you have told of liberation, Brahmana, extinction, the supreme happiness.
We have heard that those who are freed here, free of merit and sin, enter the god of a thousand rays.
Ah, the eternal dharma of liberation is hard to practise, leaving which all the gods became eaters of offerings to gods and ancestors.
Do Brahma, Rudra, Shakra the slayer of Bala, the sun, the lord of stars, wind, fire, Varuna, space, earth and the other dwellers of heaven
not know the dissolution that is made for themselves? Then by that they have taken the fixed, imperishable, unchanging way.
Cut this doubt of mine, brahmana, planted in my heart like a thorn, by telling the Itihasa; my curiosity is great.
How were the gods said to be sharers in the rites, twice-born, and why are the dwellers of heaven worshipped at sacrifices, Brahmana?
And those who take a share at sacrifices, best of the twice-born, when they sacrifice with great sacrifices, to whom do they give a share?

[Vaishampayana said:] Ah, lord of men, a most hidden question has been asked by you; it cannot be answered easily by one who has not practised austerity, nor by one ignorant of the Veda, nor one ignorant of the Puranas.
Then there was a king named Oghavan, grandfather of Nriga; his daughter was Oghavati, and his son Ogharatha.
Hearing that Angirasa had made an agreement with the king of the gods, King Marutta then took on anger.
This is my eighth meal-time since I last ate, tiger of the Kurus, so that I cannot move.
For he knew all of it then: what Gandhari had said to him before, and what Durvasas had said when he was smeared with the leavings of the pudding; Krishna remembered that too.
And your brothers are not in hell, Partha, lord of men; this is an illusion produced by Indra, king of the gods, Mahendra.
